more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Magnesium silicate is a broad legacy entry retained alongside the more specific E553a and E553b entries. The EU specifications distinguish synthetic magnesium silicate and magnesium trisilicate from natural talc. These are fine mineral-type powders with separately defined compositions and quality requirements. Their listed food role includes reducing caking in powders. A description or assessment of talc alone cannot establish the properties of every magnesium-silicate preparation.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA could not assess food-use safety because the toxicology data were insufficient in 2018.
The former shared silicate intake limit was considered obsolete.
